newsitem.title: THAILAND: Finance One, Thai Danu sign merger pact.
newsitem.headline: Finance One, Thai Danu sign merger pact.

text.p: Thailand's largest finance firm Finance One Plc and Thai Danu Bank Plc signed an agreement to merge on Friday, taking the first step towards the biggest marraige ever in the country's financial sector.
The managements of both companies hailed the memorandum of understanding as a corporate milestone that would create a strong institution able to pursue universal banking business.

They said the new entity, which will be called Thai Danu Bank, had the blessing of the central bank and the finance ministry which pledged to provide any necessary liquidity during the merger process, expected to take between six and nine months.

"I have confidence in the quality of the management and assets of Finance One and I believe market concern over its problems have been overplayed," Thai Danu president Pornsanong Tuchinda told a press conference.

He was referring to market talk in the weeks ahead of the merger announcement early this month that Finance One had run into cashflow problems partly because of its exposure to the ailing Thai property sector after an aggressive expansion during the first half of this decade.

"Finance One's position is not worse off compared with other companies in the industry," Pornsanong said. "There should be a distinction between fundamentals and confidence. I think Finance One's problems reflect a systemic risk for finance business ... especially given to its size and high profile."
Pornsanong said the merger would elevate his bank from 12th to ninth in Thailand's rankings and boost its quality assets to 190 billion baht ($7.3 billion).
Analysts said the size of assets mentioned by Pornsanong indicated the two parties may be prepared to write down 20-30 billion baht of Finance One's weak assets.
Finance One said its assets stood at 102.4 billion baht at the end of 1996 against 119.6 billion for Thai Danu.
The two firms said the merger process would start with their auditors spending about one month assessing their respective assets before determining the terms of a share swap.

Analysts estimated that 26 percent of Finance One's loans had been extended to the property sector and another 21 percent to hire-purchase business, including loans to private individuals' to buy cars.

They said Finance One's consolidated non-performing loans stood at about 5.2 billion baht, or 5.4 percent of total lending at the end of 1996, up from 4.1 billion or 4.3 percent of total loans a year ago.

Central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond said the merged bank would need to divest Finance One's hire-purchase operation, probably to one of its affiliates, because Thai banks are not licensed to undertake such business.

Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan, who witnessed the signing of the memorandum, said the government would inject liquidity into the two firms if bearish market sentiment caused them any cashflow problems.
He added the merger would serve as a model for future similar alliances among Thai banks and finance firms and that the government would encourage such moves.
